why: B is Corollary 6.8 on a compact (Hausdorff, second countable) manifold modelled on ℝⁿ: a bounded smooth f is approximated uniformly within ε by smooth g without degenerate critical points whose derivatives of order ≤ k, measured in finitely many maximal-atlas charts on compact pieces, are ε-close to those of f. A ⇒ B: A's approximation clause (any model E, any smooth coordinate systems y_j into any E', compact K_j ⊆ target) with E = E' = ℝⁿ, y_j = φ_j, K_j = φ_j(C_j); A bounds the derivatives of (g − f)∘y⁻¹, B those differences (new Glue.iteratedFDeriv_sub_comp_symm). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: A's first clause ae_isMorseFunction_add_inner_comp (for any, possibly non-compact, M and any embedding e with injective differential, f + ⟪a, e⟫ is Morse for a.e. a) is the engine of Milnor's proof and is not a consequence of an existence statement on compact M. A's boundedness hypothesis is absent (automatic on compact M).
